# Field

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server, with only its interactive part in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

Around any form control that needs a visible label, a hint or an error. Field writes the label,
the hint and the error, and hands the control the ids that tie them together, in the server
HTML, before any script runs. There is no Label component: the label is this prop.

**Two exports.** The generated Import block below prints `Field` alone; copy this line:

```tsx
import { Field, FieldLive } from 'topclassui'
```

**In a server file**, `Field`. Its child is a function that receives the control object and
spreads it onto the control:

```tsx
<Field name="email" label="Email" hint="We never share it" required>
  {(control) => <Input {...control} type="email" autoComplete="email" />}
</Field>
```

**In a client file**, `FieldLive`: the same props and the same server HTML. Given no `error`, it
shows the one the nearest `FormAction` returned for its `name`:

```tsx
export function SubscribeFields() {
  return (
    <FieldLive name="email" label="Email" required>
      {(control) => <Input {...control} type="email" />}
    </FieldLive>
  )
}
```

**The control object** is `{ id, name, required, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-invalid }`
(`FieldControl`). Every one of the eleven controls takes it as it is:

| Control | Where it lands | Named by |
|---|---|---|
| Input, Textarea | all on the native element | the `<label for>`, and `aria-labelledby` |
| Switch, Checkbox | the id and the ARIA on the button; `name` and `required` on Base UI's hidden input, `aria-required` on the button | both |
| RadioGroupRoot, SegmentedControlRoot | the ARIA and the id on the `radiogroup`; `name` and `required` to Base UI | `aria-labelledby` |
| Slider | the label and the description on the range input; `aria-invalid` on the group; `required` dropped | `aria-labelledby` |
| NumberField, Select, Combobox | the id moves to the input or the trigger, and the ARIA with it | both |
| OTPField | the id and the ARIA on the first cell | both |

**The ids.** The control takes `id`, or one from `useId()`; the label is `<id>-label`, the hint
`<id>-hint` and the error `<id>-err`. Never from `name`: two Fields may share one (a checkbox
group, two subscribe forms on a page). A page that links to a field (`#email`, an error summary
of its own) passes `id`. So `id` is the control's, never the root's: the line under the props
table that lists `id` among the root's attributes does not apply here.

**The description** is the hint's id and then the error's, only those rendered. **`error`** is
one message or the array Zod's `fieldErrors` gives; each message is a line, after a warning icon
that is only seen. With a message the control is `aria-invalid="true"`; `invalid` overrides that
either way. The error is no live region: it arrives with the page, and after a FormAction the
focus goes to the first invalid control.

**`required`** passes `required` to the control, which says so to a screen reader (`required` on
a native one, `aria-required` on a Checkbox, a Switch and the two groups). The asterisk is only
seen.

**`inline`** puts the control first and the label beside it, with the hint and the error under
the label: for a Checkbox or a Switch, where a click on the label toggles the box. In a
right-to-left page the box sits at the right.

**FieldLive and a FormAction.** An error from the form goes once the field's value changes and
comes back with the action's next answer; a click that changes nothing keeps it. It compares what
the form would send under `name` (`FormData`), read after every `input`, `change`, `click` and
`keyup` inside the field, a press in a portaled popup included. An `error` you pass is yours: it
stays until you drop it.

**On a RadioGroup, a SegmentedControl and a Slider** the label's `for` points at an element no
label can name, so a click on the label does nothing there; `aria-labelledby` names the group.

### What Base UI gives

Nothing: Field does not use Base UI's Field (choice 6). Base UI's links its label and description
only after hydration, drops a caller's `id` from the server HTML, cannot wire a native Input or
Textarea, and renames every radio of a group to the field's label.

### Not built

A Label export (choice 1); an element child, cloned with the control object (choice 8); `size`;
an "optional" word; a counter; Fieldset; any check in the browser beyond the browser's own.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Field } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Required: `children`, `label`, `name`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | **yes** | `(control: FieldControl) => ReactNode` | - | Called with the control object, which the control spreads: `(control) => <Input {...control} />`. |
| `label` | **yes** | `ReactNode` | - | The visible name of the control. |
| `name` | **yes** | `string` | - | The control's name, and the key of its errors in a FormAction's answer. |
| `error` | no | `FieldError` | - | One message or several, read after the hint; with one, the control is invalid unless `invalid` says otherwise. |
| `hint` | no | `ReactNode` | - | Text under the control that describes it: the first id of the control's aria-describedby. |
| `id` | no | `string` | - | The control's id; without it `useId()` makes one. Pass it when a page links to the field. |
| `inline` | no | `boolean` | `false` | The control first and the label beside it, the hint and the error under the label: for a Checkbox or a Switch. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | - | Sets aria-invalid on the control. Without it, true when error holds a message and false when it holds none. |
| `required` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Passes required to the control, which tells a screen reader, and shows an asterisk that is only seen. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
